native_retrieval.title: Openers, Mahedi And Rishad Help Bangladesh Keep Series Alive - Telecom Asia Sport
native_retrieval.snippet: # Openers, Mahedi And Rishad Help Bangladesh Keep Series Alive. Saif Hassan and Tanzid Hasan laid the platform before Mohammad Saifuddin's late onslaught and a spin squeeze sealed a 34-run win to level the series. Bangladesh kept the three-match T20I series alive with a commanding 34-run victory over Zimbabwe in Bulawayo, setting up a winner-takes-all decider. Their innings had two contrasting halves: a record opening stand of 120 between Saif Hassan and Tanzid Hasan, followed by a dramatic collapse, before Mohammad Saifuddin's extraordinary final-over assault lifted them to 186 for 5. Mahedi Hasan and Rishad Hossain dominated the middle overs, sharing seven wickets as Bangladesh bowled the hosts out for 152. Sikandar Raza broke the opening stand by bowling Saif, Richard Ngarava removed Tanzid and Towhid Hridoy in quick succession, and Brad Evans dismissed Parvez Hossain Emon and Nurul Hasan as Bangladesh lost five wickets for just 21 runs. 1.Openers Cash In On Zimbabwe's Generosity2.Collapse Checks Bangladesh Before Saifuddin Explodes3.Mahedi And Rishad Choke Zimbabwe4.Burl Fights, But Zimbabwe Fall Short.

english_retrieval.title: 'For India's future': Shubman Gill urges compassion, mutual respect amid student protests | Off the field News - The Times of India
english_retrieval.snippet: NEW DELHI: India Test and ODI captain Shubman Gill has spoken out amid the ongoing student protests over repeated exam paper leaks, urging compassion, mutual respect and a renewed focus on safeguarding the interests of students.In a message shared on his Instagram story on Thursday, Gill stressed that India's youth deserve every opportunity to pursue their dreams and help build the country's future. "As a young Indian, I believe our generation deserves every opportunity to learn, dream and shape the future we all aspire to," Gill wrote.His statement comes against the backdrop of widespread protests in several parts of the country, where students have taken to the streets demanding accountability over repeated examination paper leaks. I hope we move forward with compassion, mutual respect and keeping the best interests of every student at heart."He concluded his message with a simple but powerful appeal: "For India's future."Gill's comments add the voice of one of the country's biggest sporting stars to the growing conversation around ensuring fairness and trust in India's education system.
